what_it_does: When a company rents out AI language-model inference (the process of generating text responses) on cloud servers, customers want a guarantee that their data stays private. NVIDIA's H100 chip supports a hardware-enforced private computing zone — a walled-off area inside the GPU where code and data are encrypted so even the cloud provider cannot snoop. The catch is that encrypting data flowing in and out of that zone slows throughput by up to 88% for large models, because the encryption happens in lockstep with the computation. PipeLLM hides this encryption cost by predicting which data will need to be encrypted next — based on how language models predictably generate tokens and access their running memory — and starts encrypting it early, in parallel with ongoing computation. When the prediction is wrong, a lightweight fallback mechanism corrects it without any error in the output.
